changes.detail: get_or_compute treats a key as a hit when the raw Redis value is present (not None), so falsy values (0, '', [], {}, False, null) are served from cache
LRUCache.get moves the key to most-recent on a hit so reads protect entries from eviction
dumps uses a JSON default hook that serializes datetime/date as ISO 8601 strings; other unsupported types still raise TypeError
Added test_get_or_compute_caches_falsy_value_fake_client (6 params) using an in-memory fake Redis client so the fix is exercised without a Redis server
pytest cache created by test runs (gitignored)
Python bytecode caches created by test runs (gitignored)

testing.when: with redis_cache.py fix temporarily stashed, to confirm new tests catch the bug

side_effects.detail: No Redis server is available in this environment, so the 3 Redis integration tests in tests/test_redis_cache.py were skipped; fix #1 is verified only via the new fake-client tests, not against real Redis.
Behaviour change: a cached JSON null is now also treated as a hit by get_or_compute (previously it recomputed).

summary: Fixed all three issues: get_or_compute now caches falsy values (it checks for a missing key rather than whether the value is truthy), LRUCache.get refreshes recency, and serializers.dumps writes datetime/date as ISO 8601 strings. Previously failing LRU and serializer tests now pass. Added fake-client tests for get_or_compute. Full suite: 50 passed, 3 skipped (Redis not available).
